examples.solution_text:
(a) Multiply both parts by $100$.
$3.45:8.1=345:810$
Divide both by $15$.
$345:810=23:54$
(b) Multiply all three parts by $10$.
$1.2:2.6:4.4=12:26:44$
Divide all three by $2$.
$12:26:44=6:13:22$

(a) Both denominators are $12$. Multiply both parts by $12$.
$\frac{7}{12}:\frac{11}{12}=7:11$
(b) The lowest common denominator is $18$.
$\frac{5}{6}:\frac{7}{9}=\frac{15}{18}:\frac{14}{18}$
Multiply both parts by $18$.
$\frac{15}{18}:\frac{14}{18}=15:14$
Both final ratios are already simplest.

Write both parts as fractions.
$1.35=\frac{135}{100}=\frac{27}{20}$
$\frac{3}{5}=\frac{12}{20}$
Multiply both parts by $20$.
$\frac{27}{20}:\frac{12}{20}=27:12$
Divide both by $3$: $27:12=9:4$.

Write the mixed numbers as fractions.
$2\frac{2}{3}=\frac{8}{3}$ and $1\frac{3}{4}=\frac{7}{4}$.
The lowest common denominator is $12$.
$\frac{8}{3}:\frac{7}{4}=\frac{32}{12}:\frac{21}{12}$
Multiply both parts by $12$: $32:21$.
There is no common factor greater than $1$.

Write all three parts as fractions.
$0.45=\frac{45}{100}=\frac{9}{20}$
The lowest common denominator is $20$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{7}{10}:\frac{9}{20}:\frac{4}{5}\\&=\frac{14}{20}:\frac{9}{20}:\frac{16}{20}\end{aligned}$
Multiply every part by $20$: $14:9:16$.
The HCF of all three parts is $1$.

The lowest common denominator is $6$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{2}{3}:\frac{5}{6}:\frac{1}{2}\\&=\frac{4}{6}:\frac{5}{6}:\frac{3}{6}\end{aligned}$
Multiply every part by $6$.
$\frac{4}{6}:\frac{5}{6}:\frac{3}{6}=4:5:3$
The HCF of all three parts is $1$.

Write the mixed numbers as improper fractions.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}1\frac{1}{3}:2\frac{2}{3}:3\frac{1}{3}\\&=\frac{4}{3}:\frac{8}{3}:\frac{10}{3}\end{aligned}$
Multiply every part by the common denominator, $3$.
$\frac{4}{3}:\frac{8}{3}:\frac{10}{3}=4:8:10$
Divide every part by the HCF, $2$.
$4:8:10=2:4:5$

methods.description: Multiply every part by the same power of 10 to obtain whole numbers, then divide every part by the HCF. This applies to two-part and three-part ratios.

examples.derivation: 0.45 = 9/20; converting the other parts gives 14/20 : 9/20 : 16/20. Clearing denominator 20 gives 14:9:16, whose HCF is 1. The formatting change preserves the original mathematics and prose and correctly adds an invisible equals-sign gutter.

The lowest common denominator is 6: 2/3 : 5/6 : 1/2 becomes 4/6 : 5/6 : 3/6. Multiplying every part by 6 gives 4:5:3, whose HCF is 1. This follows image38's three-part fraction scaffold with different values.

The mixed numbers become 4/3 : 8/3 : 10/3. Multiplying every part by 3 gives 4:8:10; dividing by HCF 2 gives 2:4:5. This follows image39's mixed-number conversion and denominator-clearing sequence with different values.
